proposal.name: Replay known bugs and label sampled passes

issue_plan.name: Replay known bugs and label sampled passes
issue_plan.summary: Four plumbing pull requests add sampled-state coverage, ratified bug classifications, TLC-derived replay requests, and TypeScript/Python replay. Required replays must exercise real code and reject the bug's path; reproduced or incomplete replays block the gate. Unclassified legacy bugs retain model checks without replay or a new gate failure, labeled "not replayed: not classified" in receipts, JSON and dashboard; new proposals classify every bug, and only ratified current bugs require replay. Each step updates current documentation; the merger records the new reporting, classification and replay decisions, without builds rewriting decisions or existing ratified locks.

issues.title: Show sampled state coverage beside passing checks
issues.body:
Issue #789 exposed a misleading pass: a TypeScript driver sampled 100 runs of 200 steps in a 320,532-state model, missed two known bugs, and the receipt and dashboard still presented an unqualified pass. Make that limited coverage visible before the following issues add replay.

Report the exact number of distinct model states reached by checked sampled runs over TLC's distinct reachable-state count at the same ratified bounds, and display that fraction and a percentage. Use the existing conformance.Result.States and ModelStates evidence and canonical state deduplication, not runs, steps, transition counts, the dashboard's compact graph, or driver-supplied percentages. Count repeated visits once; unreferenced state-table entries are not reached states and cannot inflate coverage. Keep per-invocation coverage for existing Python applications and per-check component evidence; do not add counts from overlapping runs or unrelated component models to manufacture project coverage. Keep deterministic replay evidence separate when it is added later, so a replay does not inflate the reported random-sample share.

Put the literal word "sampled" immediately beside a passing code/conformance result with less than full state coverage, including the Markdown receipt's headline and conformance rows, existing Python and component receipt rows, and the dashboard's project cards, variants, tables and evidence pages. Carry the qualification and exact counts in JSON for consumers. A receipt with an independent successful proof keeps that proof claim, while its partial conformance result is still labeled sampled. Derive the display from evidence, including older receipts; stale assurance strings cannot hide partial coverage. Do not mutate archived reports or change their fingerprints merely by rendering them.

Use exact integer comparisons for full coverage. Near-full coverage must not round to a displayed 100% while remaining incomplete. A sampled run that happens to reach every state still does not establish proof, exhaustive exploration, every transition, or every step tried. Preserve the existing stronger requirements for "tested in every state", independent proof qualification, failed attempt checks and overall gate failure. Missing, zero or inconsistent model totals yield an explicit unknown/unavailable coverage indication, never a fabricated percentage or exhaustive claim. A pass without sufficient coverage evidence must not appear as a fully covered pass.

Relevant production paths are internal/conformance/conformance.go, internal/verify/verify.go, internal/verify/python_application_report.go, internal/verify/component_conformance.go, internal/receipt/receipt.go, internal/receipt/python_application.go, internal/receipt/component_evidence.go, internal/dashboard/dashboard.go, internal/dashboard/evidence_page.go and internal/dashboard/web/app.js. Reuse the shared receipt/evidence rendering where it already supplies the dashboard. Inspect internal/receipt/assurance_accept_test.go, internal/dashboard/assurance_accept_test.go, internal/receipt/shared_text_702_accept_test.go, internal/dashboard/assurance_775_accept_test.go, internal/dashboard/code_label_780_test.go and internal/dashboard/evidence_pages_786_test.go. Preserve existing proof and exhaustive qualifications; deliberately update only assertions and output goldens that pin an unqualified partial pass, naming every existing test that needs edits in the child plan.

Acceptance must cover a partial successful sample, canonical duplicate visits and unreferenced states, an almost-full fraction, full state coverage without exhaustive mode, missing totals, failed conformance, independent successful proof, old report JSON, and separate Python/component invocations. Exercise the rendered dashboard and receipt, not only a helper or a search for a string in source. Confirm that changing checked counts affects evidence identity where applicable, while rendering and JSON round trips preserve it.

Update SPEC.md and docs/gate.md to describe the exact coverage and qualification rules. Keep README.md's front-page explanation and gate table accurate with a short sampled-check qualification and a link to docs/gate.md, staying within 400 lines. This intentionally changes the presentation pinned by the old partial-pass tests. It rests on D-0024, D-0029, D-0043, D-0082, D-0088, D-0163, D-0170, D-0185, D-0122 and D-0294; the merger records #789's new display rule, and new or changed SPEC bullets cite their grounding decisions. Run affected Go and browser tests and the existing PR CI integration and affected real Python/TLAPS lanes.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Bind current-code bug obligations to ratification and TLC paths
issues.body:
After sampled-coverage reporting, add #789's ratified bug classifications and TLC replay obligations in one plumbing PR. project.Statement currently has only name, kind, says, expect and its TLA+ pin; verify.Run adds each bug action to Next, retaining a count and optional trace filename.

Add a bug-only code_behavior classification with explicit current and hypothetical values. New modeled proposals must classify each bug, and the formalization prompt must mark a bug current when the issue, unchanged code or its tests say the code has it, rather than treating it as merely a plausible mutation. Show the classification in the proposal and amendment comparison. Carry it into the lock, proposal hash, ratification checks and the report's bug evidence. Changing or removing it is a visible ratified-statement change, not a builder-editable manifest option. Validate its kind and values, and preserve omitted-field serialization and hashes for old locks. Do not edit existing pinned statements or ratified.lock files in this repository.

Legacy bugs without code_behavior keep today's meaning: the model must catch the bug, and nothing replays it. Existing checks, including sampled existing-code checks, must not fail for missing classification or require an amendment to keep checking. The receipt, its JSON and dashboard say "not replayed: not classified" beside each; never count it as replayed. Do not infer a classification from absence or prose. Hypothetical bugs retain only the model-strength check. Only a bug ratified as current creates a mandatory code replay obligation for driver-based checking; no missing adapter, driver option, exhausted random budget, or switch to an exhaustive declaration may silently discard that obligation. Go's existing agreement/explorer path is unchanged by this driver feature. Until the following adapter issues implement execution, affected obligations fail with a named replay-unavailable result. Model-only proposal checks still check the model and prepare the obligation without claiming any code replay.

Retain each required bug's fresh TLC counterexample in memory/private owned storage even when verify.Run has no outDir. Bind it to the staged model and sibling includes, the exact statement/classification, expected violation, ratified bounds and pinned tools. Derive a deterministic ordered replay request from that counterexample: the initial state, every prefix transition, concrete action and arguments, the offending operation, and the expected states. Do not invent a short path from sampling or permit the driver to substitute one. TLC must establish the action/argument interpretation of every edge against the bug-augmented model; its human-readable action labels and line numbers alone are insufficient when parameters or aliases are ambiguous. Preserve model values versus strings, sets versus sequences, function keys and exact integers; the display-oriented tlc.ParseValue conversion is not a lossless replay encoding.

Define and test a versioned request/result contract for the following adapters, with identities for the bug, path and invocation, ordered observed calls/states, and complete/refused/reproduced/failed outcomes. The gate owns the requested path and verdict. A successful replay must show an actually attempted offending operation rejects the forbidden behavior after the required prefix is reproduced. A changed initial state, skipped setup step, missing dispatch, arbitrary exception, premature stop, stale result or fabricated refusal is not success. A model-allowed alternative produced by the actual offending call may reject the forbidden transition, but must itself be checked. Retain temporal loop/stutter information; if an obligation cannot be translated and checked as an executable counterexample, fail it explicitly rather than treating a finite prefix as proof of liveness or silently dropping it. This issue does not add a new temporal prover.

Expose pending/failed replay obligations separately from "the model caught the bug" in JSON, Markdown and dashboard bug evidence, including unclassified status for older reports. Unclassified bugs neither count as replayed nor mask unmet current-bug obligations. Fingerprint stable replay inputs and results, excluding private paths and transient process IDs. Keep independently successful model/proof evidence, while the overall code gate cannot pass with an unmet mandatory replay.

Inspect internal/project/project.go, internal/formalize/formalize.go, prompt.go and diff.go, internal/verify/verify.go and liveness.go, internal/tlc/parse.go and trace.go, ratification/scope comparisons and existing receipt/dashboard bug rendering. Existing tests include internal/formalize/formalize_test.go, internal/formalize/diff_test.go, internal/scope/scope_test.go, internal/tlc/tlc_test.go, internal/tlc/value_test.go, internal/verify/liveness_integration_test.go, internal/verify/assurance_accept_test.go, internal/dashboard/evidence_pages_786_test.go and the Python gate admission/design-obligation fixtures. Name every existing fixture or assertion needing edits in the child plan; classify new-proposal fixtures as required, retain unclassified legacy gate fixtures and preserve their refusal cases.

Acceptance must demonstrate hash/diff sensitivity to classification, unchanged legacy hashes, new proposals rejecting missing classifications, otherwise passing legacy sampled gates still passing and model-strength failures still failing, the exact not-replayed label in receipt/JSON/dashboard, no replay calls or counts for unclassified bugs, mixed classifications, complete independently bound paths for two different bugs, parameterized/repeated actions and typed values, rejection of malformed or ambiguous paths, no-outDir retention, current-bug obligations blocking a green gate, and model-only checking without code execution. Use command-boundary stand-ins for unit tests and the existing integration lane for pinned TLC path extraction.

Update SPEC.md, docs/gate.md and the proposal/ratification explanation in docs/factory.md for the behavior actually delivered and its temporary adapter-unavailable result. Keep README.md accurate if its gate explanation now needs a short replay-obligation qualification. This rests on D-0011, D-0013, D-0017, D-0026, D-0029, D-0054, D-0069, D-0071, D-0105, D-0122, D-0294 and D-0333. The merger records the new ratified classification, legacy compatibility and replay-evidence decisions; the plumbing build does not write decisions/. This issue must land as one complete plumbing PR, without another issue plan.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Replay TLC bug paths through TypeScript and ordinary Python drivers
issues.body:
Issue #789's motivating failure was an existing TypeScript hook: ReplayCompletedTask and ReuseRecoveredName both required delivery, reload, recovery and a second delivery, and a fixed-weight random driver never tried them. After the preceding issue adds ratified bug classifications and TLC-derived replay obligations, implement their execution for ordinary TypeScript, existing TypeScript and ordinary Python drivers in one plumbing pull request. These routes share the command-based conformance execution and recording infrastructure. Existing Python applications use their authenticated adapter in the next issue and must continue refusing required replay until that adapter is available.

Add gate-owned replay harnesses and a documented driver interface for initializing real code, dispatching each concrete model operation/argument list, and reading back the resulting state. Stage the fresh TLC replay request read-only into the existing throwaway sandbox and run every required bug independently from its specified initial state, regardless of the driver's random seed, step count, weights or whether random sampling found the prefix. The harness owns sequencing and completion records. Map the bug action to the actual application operation that can exhibit it; it must not be a synthetic mutation of a driver-owned state or a special callback that returns "refused" without trying the code. Preserve the existing TypeScript requirement to import every named existing-code selection and the driver review's checks of real calls and read-back.

Keep normal sampling and its evidence, then independently check each replay's observed states and operations against the request and model using the shared contract. Reproducing a required forbidden path fails the public gate and names the bug, offending step and observed state. Rejecting that behavior through a real operation passes that obligation only after a valid matching prefix and a checked refusal or model-allowed alternative. Missing/unimplemented dispatch, null to skip a required operation, altered initial state, unexpected divergence, an unrecognized exception, missing/truncated/duplicate/stale output, a failed process, timeout or cleanup failure cannot count as a refusal. Every current bug is required; one refused bug cannot mask another reproduced or unfinished bug. Retain all existing model, build, proof, conformance, tried-step and larger-bound requirements. Replay does not turn a sample into exhaustive evidence.

Wire the check into verify.Run and the factory's ordinary gate path, not merely a standalone driver API or prompt. Preserve sandbox dependency images, no-network execution, selected existing source hashes, fixed random defaults, resource limits, marker validation and streaming recording ownership. No ordinary check may require network installation. New replay imports must not accidentally make Explores treat a sampled driver as exhaustive under D-0088. Keep old drivers with no required current-code bug obligations working; classified current obligations without the new interface fail with actionable diagnostics. No changes to the application under test are needed.

Return per-bug replay results and diagnostics through the shared report, receipt and dashboard evidence added in the previous issue. Preserve their stable fingerprints through JSON round trips. Keep random-sample counts separate from deterministic replay counts and rejected buggy terminal states. Update synthesis instructions and the read-only driver review instructions so generated drivers implement the interface and reviewers inspect the concrete real-code operation bindings.

Read internal/verify/language.go, existing.go, harness.go, recording.go, the embedded harnesses and internal/synth/prompt.go and review.go. Existing compatibility checks include internal/verify/existing_test.go, existing_integration_test.go, harness_test.go, harness_integration_test.go, sandbox_integration_test.go and gate_recording_stream_accept_test.go. The latter's Docker fake checks DRIVER, INVARIANT_TRACES=/out/traces.json, INVARIANT_RUNS=1000, INVARIANT_STEPS=40, INVARIANT_SEED=1, image/mount arguments and @@invariant command markers; update the fake only for the deliberate replay additions and retain those assertions. Inspect Python launcher/dependency and synthesis tests before naming the child-plan files.

Acceptance must use a self-contained fixture reproducing the two #789 sequences, without fetching ask3d. Arrange for the random trace to miss both bugs, assert it passes ordinary conformance, and then show the actual gate fails independently for each buggy implementation through deterministic replay. A corrected implementation must reject each forbidden path and allow the gate to pass. Exercise both TypeScript sandbox routes and ordinary Python, multiple bugs in one run, a missing replay implementation, omitted second bug, skipped prefix, unexpected exception, malformed/stale evidence, cancellation and cleanup. At least the integration regression must execute the actual driver and code through the pinned tools, not merely make a fake emit a chosen verdict. Use the existing PR integration lane; do not introduce a new workflow.

Update SPEC.md, docs/gate.md and the relevant driver guidance in docs/factory.md; keep README.md's concise description and gate table accurate and within 400 lines. Describe only these implemented adapters, and keep the existing-Python limitation explicit until the next issue lands. This rests on D-0024, D-0029, D-0054, D-0082, D-0085, D-0087, D-0088, D-0105, D-0111, D-0122, D-0294 and D-0333, plus the preceding issue's recorded replay decision. The merger records any additional execution decision; the build does not change decisions/ or existing ratified locks.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Replay known bug paths through authenticated Python application checks
issues.body:
Complete issue #789 for existing Python applications after the preceding issues have delivered sampled-coverage reporting, ratified bug classifications, TLC-derived replay requests and the command-based driver adapters. Existing Python is a separate execution path: its gate-owned collector observes selected real calls, binds them to an invocation and source snapshots, reads state back from the application, and authenticates completed observation streams. Implement required bug replay through that path in one plumbing pull request, preserving its evidence boundary.

Provide an application-driver replay interface that dispatches the requested concrete operations through the existing functional, instance and module lifecycle facilities, using the same selected code, surrounding entries and read-back declarations as conformance. The collector, not the application driver, must bind the bug/path identity, operation order, actual selected calls, before/after states, refusal outcomes and completion to the fresh invocation. Retain the existing module reload/recovery and held-call rules where they are used. This must work with explicit component selections and with legacy existing-Python selections. Current-bug obligations cannot be bypassed by changing the conformance mode; sampled and supported exhaustive application invocations must honor them.

Use the common replay verdict rules: each required prefix must execute from its requested initial state, the offending real operation must be attempted, reproducing the forbidden path fails, and only an observed checked refusal or valid alternative rejects that path successfully. Preserve declared-refusal exception semantics and the distinction between model-bound omissions and real refusals. A missing call, unbound target, wrong driver or entry, changed snapshot, wrong invocation, replayed authentication stream, arbitrary exception, mismatched state, missing completion, failed process, timeout or failed cleanup must never become a passing refusal. Unsupported executable bindings produce a named failure, not a fallback to unauthenticated JSON or ordinary process success.

Integrate this into public preflight, session preparation and verify.Run, removing the previous step's adapter-unavailable refusal only for configurations now implemented. Run all required bug obligations against the same staged application/model generation and admitted dependency image used by the other checks. Preserve isolation, startup/import policy, private transport freshness, limits, cancellation and cleanup. Keep independent successful test/proof/conformance evidence when another check fails, while missing or failed mandatory replay prevents the overall gate from passing. Public supplied component-evidence attribution must not fabricate gate replay success.

Record actual executions and replay outcomes with their source/model/bounds/tool identities in application and bug evidence, JSON/Markdown and dashboard presentation. They must survive JSON round trips and affect stable fingerprints when inputs, operations or observed results change. Temporary paths, authentication tokens and local container IDs stay out of portable identity. Do not count deterministic replays again as random sampled coverage, or confuse these bug replays with the exploration-prefix replays already filtered by python_application_recording.go. Preserve streaming conversion and exact integer/module-value semantics.

Relevant code is internal/verify/python_application_gate.go, python_application_session.go, python_application_execution.go, python_application_observer.py, python_application_observations.go, python_application_recording.go and python_application_report.go, plus existing application/component receipt rendering. Inspect internal/verify/python_application_observations_accept_test.go, python_application_gate_accept_test.go, declared_refusal_accept_test.go, declared_refusal_wire_regression_test.go, the module/hold replay tests, gate_recording_stream_accept_test.go, internal/verify/internal/pythongatetest and internal/verify/pythongate/gate_test.go before naming files. Preserve original authentication, refusal, continuity, process and cleanup assertions; name any existing fixture that the new classification or invocation protocol requires changing. Keep the local GateFailures and GateFingerprints scheduling rules from AGENTS.md.

Acceptance must exercise actual selected Python code with both explicit and legacy selections: a random sample misses a delivery/reload/recovery/redelivery bug, required replay exposes it, and a repaired implementation rejects it. Cover two required bugs, parameter arguments, module lifecycle continuity, exact declared exceptions, missing dispatch/calls, invalid or stale authenticated evidence, premature exit, cancellation, fingerprints and independent evidence preservation. Test that a driver cannot turn a missing replay into successful conformance and that every relevant invocation is accounted for. Unit tests use the existing local runner/fakes; the affected real Python opt-in and existing integration suites run in PR CI, along with affected TLAPS checks. No new CI files are required.

Update SPEC.md, docs/gate.md and docs/python.md for the completed replay behavior, removing the temporary adapter limitation and documenting the application interface and evidence. Update README.md only as needed to keep its short overall claim accurate, within 400 lines. This rests on D-0029, D-0054, D-0170, D-0181, D-0183, D-0185, D-0199, D-0279, D-0284, D-0329, D-0333, D-0105, D-0122 and D-0294, together with the replay decision recorded for the preceding issues. The merger records additional execution decisions; the plumbing build does not write decisions/ or existing ratified locks. This finishes all adapters and reporting required by #789, with no unplanned follow-up.

Kind: plumbing
